meta.label: ROLE D. Fitted and cross-validated on a very small labelled set. Exploratory; nothing here is a success claim and nothing replaces Role A's headline.

thermal_layer.label: Role A earth_features_v2_6km.parquet, MODIS MOD11A2 2019-2023, copied 2026-11-15 11:45 IST

meta.shuffled_baseline: 1000 draws, seed 20261114, Earth thermal ranks permuted across the tiles of each universe; M3 repeats the full fit per draw

entries.statement: The fit uses 4 scorable Mars positives and 201 negative units. One positive moves recall by 25 points or more.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Any fitted thermal weight is close to a guess. Fitted and cross-validated on a very small labelled set.

entries.statement: Role A's Earth thermal layer has a valid th_mean for 73.4 percent of v1 land tiles between 55S and 60N. The registered rule needs 85 percent. Tiles without a value (polar blocks and areas where the pre-registered MODIS QC rule leaves no value) are outside the universe.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: The scored universe is a subset of Earth that leaves out much of the driest land that a desert negative set would sample. D1 and D2 are NOT TESTED under the registered rule; the metrics are reported as descriptive numbers.

entries.statement: The 200 negative tiles were drawn from bare, low, near-equatorial land. They cluster in a few deserts and are not independent.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Bootstrap intervals and the false-positive rate look more certain than they are.

entries.statement: The v1 Earth file has no share of bare or sparse cover. The negative set uses NDVI median at most 0.10 and little water, ice, built or crop.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: The negatives are bare-ground tiles by a proxy, not by a land-cover class share.

entries.statement: The Earth partner of Mars thermal inertia is the rank of minus the MODIS day-minus-night swing. It is a proxy, not thermal inertia.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: A match in rank says the day-night swing is of similar rank, not that the ground has the same inertia.

entries.statement: Moon PRP temp_avg and temp_max are modelled values; the Earth partners are satellite skin temperatures from MODIS composites.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Rank within each body is compared. Absolute values cannot match: Earth has no surface near polar cold-trap temperatures.

entries.statement: Moon ice_depth is context only. The primary Moon score leaves out the illumination family; a variant with it is reported next to it.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth cannot match polar lighting, so the primary Moon score says nothing about illumination.

entries.statement: Arcadia has no centre and no thermal reference. Moon diurnal range, cold-trap share and Mars surface temperature have no source or no Earth partner.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: These properties are not scored here.
